innate.name: Self-directed initiative
innate.behavior: You start moving before the group agrees on a plan. In a meeting where everyone is still circling the question, you are the one who says 'let's try this' and begins assigning the first steps. You trust your own read of a situation over consensus, and you act on it — booking the room, sending the first message, making the call — while others are still confirming who should do what. When a peer hesitates, you fill the gap yourself rather than wait.
innate.evidence: Companion and Rob Wealth are jointly heaviest (13 and 11). The year and month stems are both Companion, the hour stem is Rob Wealth, and hidden Rob Wealth appears in the month and day branches. The Day Master is Gui water with special-pattern characteristics, and water fills seven of the eight visible characters, so the self-and-peers axis dominates the chart.

innate.name: Peer-network activation
innate.behavior: You naturally pull people into motion. When you need something done, you reach for a contact rather than a process — you text the person who knows the person, you bring two acquaintances together because they should meet, you rally a small group around a shared task without formal authority. In a new environment, you find your circle within days by talking to whoever is standing nearby, and that circle becomes your working infrastructure.
innate.evidence: Companion and Rob Wealth together carry twenty-four of the thirty-one Ten God weight points. The month and day branches both hide Rob Wealth, and the hour branch hides Companion, so the peer-and-competition axis is embedded at multiple levels of the chart, not just on the surface.

innate.name: Improvised problem-solving
innate.behavior: When a plan breaks mid-execution, you do not stop to renegotiate the plan — you patch it on the spot. A supplier cancels, and you are already calling a backup before the meeting ends. A tool fails, and you rig a workaround with what is on hand. You treat obstacles as things to route around rather than reasons to pause, and you often finish the task with a different method than the one you started with.
innate.evidence: The Output family — Eating God and Hurting Officer — sits in the hidden stems of the year, month, and day branches, with Eating God at 3 and Hurting Officer at 2. This latent output is present but underfed, so it surfaces as quick improvisation under pressure rather than sustained, visible production.

trained.name: Competitive resource-scrambling
trained.behavior: You scan for who else wants the same slot, credit, or budget, and you move to secure your share before the conversation about fairness begins. In a team project, you are the one who claims the visible deliverable early. In a job search, you apply to the same role as three people you know and treat it as a race rather than a collaboration. You track what peers are getting and adjust your own position accordingly.
trained.trained_by: An environment where resources were shared among peers and nothing was allocated by a clear authority — where the only way to get your share was to move first and hold it. The chart shows Rob Wealth at 11, nearly as heavy as Companion, and hidden Rob Wealth in both the month and day branches, meaning the competitive peer dynamic was present at the closest levels of your life, not just in the wider world.
trained.evidence: Rob Wealth weighs 11, second only to Companion at 13. Hidden Rob Wealth appears in the month branch and the day branch, and the hour stem is Rob Wealth. The Wealth family weighs zero, so the scramble is not about accumulating wealth but about securing position among peers.

trained.name: Self-reliant over-extension
trained.behavior: You take on more than one person can carry because you assume no one else will do it properly. You answer the email, fix the spreadsheet, and make the call yourself rather than delegate, and you end up working late on tasks that were never assigned to you. When someone offers help, you say yes but then redo their part anyway. The result is that you are always busy and the group's output still depends on your hands.
trained.trained_by: An environment where relying on others repeatedly failed or where asking for help was treated as a weakness. The chart shows Companion and Rob Wealth dominating while the Resource family weighs zero — no Indirect Resource or Direct Resource to draw on — so there was no structural support to lean on, and self-reliance became the default.
trained.evidence: Companion 13 and Rob Wealth 11 dominate the weights. Indirect Resource and Direct Resource both weigh zero, and the Output family is thin (Eating God 3, Hurting Officer 2), so there is little in the chart that converts effort into finished, visible output without your direct involvement.

defensive.name: Constant coordination
defensive.looks_like: You appear to be the natural leader of the group — the one who keeps everyone aligned, who knows what each person is doing, who holds the thread. Outsiders see a person who is organized, connected, and on top of things.
defensive.actual_cost: The coordination is not a choice; it is a response to the fear that if you stop, the group will fragment or someone will take your place. You spend energy tracking peers, mediating small conflicts, and re-confirming plans, and you finish the day with nothing visible to show for it. The output side — the actual deliverable — gets pushed to tomorrow, and tomorrow looks the same.
defensive.evidence: Companion and Rob Wealth together carry twenty-four of thirty-one weight points, while Eating God and Hurting Officer together carry only five. The Output family is present only in hidden stems, so visible production is structurally underfed while peer coordination is overfed.

defensive.name: Preemptive self-sufficiency
defensive.looks_like: You appear impressively capable — the person who never needs help, who figures everything out alone, who is always ready. People trust you with difficult tasks because you never seem to drop them.
defensive.actual_cost: You are running on a reserve that does not refill. Because the Resource family weighs zero, there is no structural source of replenishment — no mentor, no system, no savings of energy to draw on. Every task you take on alone drains the same tank, and the tank has no inlet. The long-term cost is that you become the bottleneck for everything you touch, and the things you actually want to build stay unfinished.
defensive.evidence: Indirect Resource and Direct Resource both weigh zero. The Wealth family also weighs zero, so there is no accumulation on either the support side or the reward side. The chart's energy is concentrated in Companion and Rob Wealth, which move outward but do not store.

one_leverage: Self-directed initiative. It is the one ability that both grows out of the chart's heaviest axis and refills your energy while you use it. Companion and Rob Wealth dominate the structure, and acting on your own read is the natural expression of that dominance — you do not have to force it, and it does not drain you the way coordination or self-sufficiency does. The leverage comes from pointing it at a single visible deliverable before the next round of peer coordination begins. The chart shows the Output family is thin and hidden, so finished, visible work is the missing piece; using your initiative to protect one deliverable — writing it down, finishing it, shipping it — converts your natural drive into something that accumulates. The luck pillars starting around age 39 and age 49 bring earth and fire into the picture, giving the output-to-wealth side something to land on, but the lever you control now is where you point the initiative you already have.
